abstract: The status of the light reactions of photosynthesis is tightly linked to subcellular physiology and metabolism. Yet, monitoring how both these levels are coordinated in living plants has remained challenging to explore. Here, we combine genetically encoded biosensors with time- and wavelength-resolved chlorophyll fluorescence spectroscopy (ChloroSpec L1) in attached Arabidopsis thaliana leaves. Stromal pHluorin2 reported a reversible, light-dependent alkalinization in a single mesophyll layer of leaf discs imaged by confocal microscopy and over the illuminated area of attached leaves recorded by ChloroSpec, where a distinct overshoot appeared at all irradiances. Measurement of the light-response dynamics of stromal MgATP2-, cytosolic pH, and cytosolic NADH/NAD+ illustrates the flexibility of the approach to different biosensors and subcellular localizations. Under prolonged fluctuating light, simultaneous recordings linked progressive stromal alkalinization and slow cytosolic NAD redox integration to wavelength-dependent shifts in photosystem II efficiency and non-photochemical quenching. By coupling programmable illumination with multiplexed metabolic and spectroscopic readouts in planta, this platform bridges cellular bioenergetics and leaf physiology to dissect photosynthetic regulation under dynamic environments.
